units.text: INT. DOLLHOUSE - CONTINUOUS
And your husband keeps the key?
units.name: MRS LINDE

units.text: Yes, always.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Krogstad must ask for his letter back unread, he must find some pretence—
units.name: MRS LINDE

units.text: But it is just at this time that Torvald generally—
units.name: NORA

units.text: You must delay him. Go in to him in the meantime. I will come back as soon as I can.
units.name: MRS LINDE

units.text: She goes out hurriedly through the hall door.
goes to HELMER’S door, opens it and peeps in.
. Torvald!
units.name: NORA

units.text: from the inner room.
. Well? May I venture at last to come into my own room again? Come along, Rank, now you will see—
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Halting in the doorway.
But what is this?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: What is what, dear?
units.name: NORA

units.text: Rank led me to expect a splendid transformation.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: in the doorway.
. I understood so, but evidently I was mistaken.
units.name: RANK

units.text: Yes, nobody is to have the chance of admiring me in my dress until tomorrow.
units.name: NORA

units.text: But, my dear Nora, you look so worn out. Have you been practising too much?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: No, I have not practised at all.
units.name: NORA

units.text: But you will need to—
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Yes, indeed I shall, Torvald. But I can’t get on a bit without you to help me; I have absolutely forgotten the whole thing.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Oh, we will soon work it up again.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Yes, help me, Torvald. Promise that you will! I am so nervous about it—all the people—. You must give yourself up to me entirely this evening. Not the tiniest bit of business—you mustn’t even take a pen in your hand. Will you promise, Torvald dear?
units.name: NORA

units.text: I promise. This evening I will be wholly and absolutely at your service, you helpless little mortal. Ah, by the way, first of all I will just—
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Goes towards the hall door.
What are you going to do there?
units.name: NORA

units.text: Only see if any letters have come.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: No, no! don’t do that, Torvald!
units.name: NORA

units.text: Why not?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Torvald, please don’t. There is nothing there.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Well, let me look.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Turns to go to the letter-box.
NORA, at the piano, plays the first bars of the Tarantella.
HELMER stops in the doorway.
Aha!
units.name: HELMER

units.text: I can’t dance tomorrow if I don’t practise with you.
units.name: NORA

units.text: going up to her.
. Are you really so afraid of it, dear?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Yes, so dreadfully afraid of it. Let me practise at once; there is time now, before we go to dinner. Sit down and play for me, Torvald dear; criticise me, and correct me as you play.
units.name: NORA

units.text: With great pleasure, if you wish me to.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Sits down at the piano.
takes out of the box a tambourine and a long variegated shawl.
She hastily drapes the shawl round her.
Then she springs to the front of the stage and calls out.
. Now play for me! I am going to dance!
units.name: NORA

units.text: HELMER plays and NORA dances.
RANK stands by the piano behind HELMER, and looks on.
as he plays.
. Slower, slower!
units.name: HELMER

units.text: I can’t do it any other way.
units.name: NORA
